title: Explain Bounded Context in microservices (DDD), its principles, advantages, and disadvantages.
keyPoints: A Bounded Context is an explicit boundary where one domain model and one ubiquitous language are consistent and unambiguous.
Inside the boundary every term has exactly one meaning; outside it the same word may mean something different.
In microservices each bounded context typically maps to one service with its own model and private database.
Contexts relate through context maps: shared kernel, customer-supplier, anti-corruption layer, and domain events.
Advantages: clear boundaries, autonomous teams, consistent language, independent evolution.
Disadvantages: model duplication, translation at borders, costly to fix if boundaries are drawn wrong early.
A bounded context is first a modeling boundary and only then a deployment boundary.

s1_definition.oneliner: A Bounded Context is an explicit boundary where one domain model and one ubiquitous language are consistent; each maps to a service with its own model and database, and contexts talk through explicit context maps.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Bounded Context** – a DDD concept defining an explicit boundary within which a domain model and ubiquitous language are consistent.
- **Ubiquitous language** – the exact words the team uses in code, docs, and conversation, consistent only inside the boundary.
- **Microservices mapping** – each bounded context becomes one service with a private database.
- **Context maps** – how contexts relate: shared kernel, customer-supplier, anti-corruption layer, domain events.
- **Key principle** – models are valid only within their context; never build one universal model for the whole enterprise.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India the word 'account' means different things to different teams. To the Deposits team it is a savings account with a balance. To the Lending team it is a loan account with principal and EMI. To the Cards team it is a credit-card account with a limit. A Bounded Context says: stop trying to force one definition on everybody. Draw a boundary around each world and let each team speak its own precise language inside its own walls. When they must talk, they translate at the border.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Bounded Contexts at National Bank of India:

  ┌─────────────────┐    events    ┌─────────────────┐
  │  DEPOSITS CTX   │─────────────►│  LENDING CTX    │
  │                 │              │                 │
  │ Account = SAV   │  FundsDebited│ Account = LOAN  │
  │ Balance, Holder │              │ Principal, EMI  │
  │                 │              │                 │
  │ Deposits DB     │              │ Lending DB      │
  └─────────────────┘              └─────────────────┘
         │                                │
         │ events                         │ events
         ▼                                ▼
  ┌─────────────────┐              ┌─────────────────┐
  │  PAYMENT CTX    │              │  CARDS CTX      │
  │                 │              │                 │
  │ Transfer, Settl │              │ Account = CARD  │
  │ Amount, Status  │              │ Limit, Due Date │
  │                 │              │                 │
  │ Payment DB      │              │ Cards DB        │
  └─────────────────┘              └─────────────────┘

  Each context: own model, own language, own database.
  Communication: domain events + anti-corruption layers.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A Bounded Context defines an explicit boundary within which one domain model and one ubiquitous language are consistent. At National Bank of India, 'account' means a deposit account to the Deposits team, a loan account to the Lending team, and a credit-card account to the Cards team. Instead of one universal Account model, each team has its own precise definition inside its own walls.

In microservices, each bounded context becomes one service with its own private database. Contexts communicate through domain events and context maps like anti-corruption layers that translate at the border. The Deposits context publishes a FundsDebited event, and the Lending context consumes it through an adapter that translates it into an EMI payment, so neither model contaminates the other.

The disadvantages are real: model duplication, translation overhead at borders, and the cost of fixing boundaries drawn wrong early. The senior point is that a bounded context is first a modeling boundary and only then a deployment boundary. Split services without domain modeling and you get technically separated services that still share concepts and still change together.

Remember one sentence: a Bounded Context is the boundary where one model and one language are consistent, and each one maps to one microservice with its own database so teams can evolve independently.
